t: The largest Mississippian centre, built from about 1050 on the Mississippi floodplain opposite present-day St Louis.
Its Monks Mound, about 30 metres high, is the largest prehistoric earthwork in the Americas.
From the late 12th century the city shrank behind a palisade, and by about 1350 it was largely abandoned.
dyk: From the centre of Cahokia’s reconstructed Woodhenge, a circle of 48 timber posts, the sun rises over Monks Mound at the spring and autumn equinoxes.
ev: Villages on the American Bottom are rebuilt to a grand plan around the Grand Plaza
Cahokia reaches its peak, with perhaps 10,000–20,000 people
A walled compound in the East St Louis precinct is burned
A palisade with bastions is built around the central precinct
Monks Mound receives its last major addition as the population falls
Cahokia Mounds becomes a UNESCO World Heritage Site

f.capital: Cahokia, around Monks Mound and the Grand Plaza (near present-day Collinsville, Illinois)
f.predecessor: Terminal Late Woodland villages of the American Bottom
f.successor: None; the region was largely abandoned (the Vacant Quarter)
